what_this_is: The persistence invariant for teardown. The owner set NO balance floor and instructed that credits be drained, which inverts the safety model: instead of protecting spend, every artifact must already be durable at every moment, so an instance dying at zero balance costs compute only and never evidence. This manifest is the proof of that invariant.

jl-vm-473501 (8x): ~/logs (serve logs, gate receipts, needle receipts, A/B ladders)
main-omp-session (471041): nothing host-only: this box IS the repo working tree, already committed and pushed

git (small, load-bearing).contents: every result.json, every metrics JSONL, the GPU telemetry CSVs, the 8x serve/gate/needle logs, models.yml
git (small, load-bearing).why: these are the files a future reader needs to re-derive or audit any published number

already-committed duplicates.why: 71 pulled files were byte-identical to files already committed in the repo - chiefly the ladder receipts, which were authored here and copied to the driver. Re-storing them would inflate the repo for zero durability gain, so the manifest PROVES the match and the copy was dropped.

files.contents: per-task agent transcripts, oracle outputs, per-trial logs across all TB2.1 arms

HF dataset (bulky, forensic).why: forensically valuable but not load-bearing; a dataset repo is the correct home for tens of MiB of blobs

deliberately_NOT_persisted.reason: 1.6 GB asciinema capture from a single task that has never resolved in any arm. It is 74 % of all job-directory bytes on the driver. The task emulates a Windows 3.11 install and spews unbounded terminal output; the recording carries no measurement and no rope signal. Excluding it also motivated the pre-registered exclusion of that task from the 512k arm on disk-safety grounds.
545 MB tmux pane dump from the same runaway task, same reasoning.
process IDs of dead processes on hosts about to be destroyed; meaningless once the host is gone.

deliberately_NOT_persisted.reason: an interactive session, not an artifact; its transcripts live under ~/.omp/agent/sessions which is not a measurement source.

deliberately_NOT_persisted.reason: contain the task's planted HF/GitHub/AWS fixture secrets, 121 matches between them. Removed rather than allow-listed; see secret_scanning_incident. None of our own credentials appear anywhere in the sweep.

invariant_statement: At the time of writing, every file on every rental is in exactly one of four states: committed to git, proven byte-identical to something already committed, uploaded to the HF dataset, or listed above with a reason. There is no unexplained residue. An instance dying now costs compute only. RE-VERIFIED after the 512k arm: the arm's own artifacts (55 result.json plus 24 metrics files) have been swept, deduped and committed, so the invariant still holds at teardown time and not merely at first sweep.

verification.how: re-run the sweep and diff against this manifest; every git-bound entry's sha256 must match the committed file, and the HF archives are addressed by repo path

final_sweep_after_the_512k_arm.oversized_reason: ladder receipts over 2 MiB that are already committed under their canonical receipts/tb21-ladder-*.json names; the driver held working copies

secret_scanning_incident.what_happened: GitHub push protection REJECTED the final sweep commit with GH013, naming a Hugging Face User Access Token inside a swept agent transcript. The push was blocked before anything reached the remote.
secret_scanning_incident.root_cause: Both files belong to the Terminal-Bench task `sanitize-git-repo`, whose entire purpose is to find and remove secrets from a git repository. Its fixtures are therefore realistic token-shaped strings, and the agent's trajectory quotes them verbatim as it works. Sweeping raw agent transcripts from a benchmark that contains secret-handling tasks will reliably trip secret scanning.

were_any_OURS.method: scanned all 767 swept files for hf_/ghp_/AKIA/sk-/xox/private-key patterns and for our real HF token's exact bytes and the Jarvis key's exact bytes. Zero matches for either of ours.
were_any_OURS.conclusion: NOT an incident with our credentials. No rotation required. The blocked strings are third-party fixtures.

secret_scanning_incident.resolution: Both files DELETED from the swept set rather than allow-listed. The unblock URL GitHub offered was deliberately NOT used: allow-listing would publish someone else's fixture secrets into a public repository, which is the wrong outcome even when the secrets are synthetic.
secret_scanning_incident.lesson: Filter raw agent transcripts for secret patterns BEFORE committing them, not after a push is rejected. The scan is cheap - seven regexes over 767 files - and push protection is the wrong place to discover it, because by then the bytes are already in a local commit that has to be rewritten.
